_comment_1: Copy this file to config/teams.json and edit the paths for your machine. Every value here is an example, not a detected fact; nothing is guessed for you.
_comment_2: ABSOLUTE path to the OpenCode CLI. Used only when 'sources' is absent or empty (single-source mode).
_comment_3: Optional OpenCode service URL, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:4096. An empty string lets the CLI use its own background service and its own auth.
_comment_4: Seconds: how often to poll, and when a card counts as stale.
_comment_5: Dashboard listener. Loopback by default; a non-loopback bind also requires --allow-external-bind.
_comment_6: Exact session ids to hide from the dashboard - never titles, agent names or substrings. Leave empty unless you really want to exclude a specific session.
_comment_7: sources[] REPLACES the single implicit source above: one entry per OpenCode installation (for example one per WSL2 distribution, plus optionally the native Windows CLI reached through interop). Each source polls independently, so a failing source only marks its own cards UNKNOWN.

sources._comment_optional: OPTIONAL: delete this whole object if you do not run OpenCode natively on Windows. WSL2 interop invokes the Windows executable directly; no Windows service, listener or extra port is created.
sources._comment_exe: Replace with the /mnt/c/... interop path of your Windows opencode.exe.

_comment_8: Team groups used when 'sources' is empty (single-source back-compat); the same five groups are also exposed as cfg.teams. Leave session_id null to DISCOVER every primary session whose worktree matches worktree_dir exactly - several primaries in one worktree become stacked cards. Pin an exact ses_* id only as a migration/compat anchor. Optional child_session_ids pins known advisory child sessions.
